slides.title: Generative Bionics Unveils Humanoid Robot with Full-Body Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT WITH FULL-BODY TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: The development of a humanoid robot with full-body tactile sensing is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Towards Artificial Nerves: Biomimetic Optical-Fiber Tactile Sensing for Robots
slides.highlight: OptiTac introduces a biomimetic tactile sensor using optical fibers as artificial nerves to achieve high spatial resolution and interpretable touch perception.

card.one_liner: OptiTac is a biomimetic tactile sensor using optical fibers to enable interpretable, high-resolution robotic touch.
card.key_idea: A one-to-one pairing of mechanical pins and optical fibers routes tactile signals to a remote camera, using image moments for analytical inference instead of deep learning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via indentations with various shapes/sizes; achieved sub-millimeter localization (RMSE ~0.4mm) and 96% shape classification accuracy using Gaussian Mixture Models.
card.limitation: Performance was tested under controlled laboratory conditions with short fibers; robustness to long-distance routing and repeated bending remains unquantified.

slides.title: MVP-Tac: A Miniaturized Dual-Modal Vision and Photoelastic Tactile Sensor for Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery
slides.tldr: DUAL-MODAL VISION AND TACTILE SENSOR FOR MINIMALLY INVASIVE SURGERY
slides.highlight: MVP-Tac integrates reflective photoelastic imaging to provide co-located vision and tactile sensing, enabling hardness classification of tumors with high accuracy.

card.one_liner: MVP-Tac is a miniaturized sensor providing co-located vision and tactile sensing for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery.
card.key_idea: Uses reflective photoelastic imaging with a semi-transparent membrane and controllable illumination to switch between visual navigation and stress-dependent tactile sensing without structured lighting.
card.evaluation: Validated via force calibration (0-2N), tissue phantoms (97% exposed/92% subdermal tumor classification accuracy), and a simulated colonoscopy with 3D luminal mapping.
card.limitation: VytaFlex elastomer causes slow recovery, early plastic deformation, and fragility under concentrated contacts, limiting repeatability and sensitivity.

slides.authors: Md Rakibul Islam Prince et al.

slides.title: FM-VLA: Force-based Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models in Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: FORCE-BASED MEMORY FOR CONTACT-RICH ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: FM-VLA introduces a force-based memory using a variational autoencoder to enable temporal context reasoning in non-Markovian, contact-rich tasks. This approach outperforms vision-based memory in visually ambiguous scenarios with minimal inference overhead.

card.one_liner: FM-VLA uses force-based memory to enable temporal reasoning for non-Markovian, contact-rich robotic manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A pretrained VAE compresses long-horizon wrench histories into compact tokens, which, combined with short-term state history, condition a flow-matching action expert.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three bimanual tasks (finding blocks, pressing buttons, wiping dishes); achieved 83.3% average success rate, significantly outperforming memoryless and vision-memory baselines.
card.limitation: The fixed 8-token VAE bottleneck may struggle with very long-horizon tasks requiring memory of hundreds of contact events.

slides.title: BayesContact: Uncertain Pose Estimation via Visuo-Tactile Proposals and Simulation-based Inference
slides.highlight: This work proposes a simulation-based inference framework for visuo-tactile pose estimation, contributing to HyECHO's goal of multimodal perception for hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: BayesContact uses simulation-based inference to fuse vision and tactile data for uncertain peg-in-hole pose estimation.
card.key_idea: A Sequential Monte Carlo framework using a graphics renderer for depth likelihoods and a physics simulator for contact likelihoods to maintain a multimodal pose belief.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-robot experiments across five geometries; showed 30% improvement in insertion success and observability over vision-only baselines.
card.limitation: Likelihood evaluations during the contact phase require physics simulations, preventing the use of Metropolis-Hastings rejuvenation for particle refinement.

slides.title: VTAP Gripper: Synergizing Fingertip Sensing and a Visuo-Tactile Active Palm for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a gripper combining a visuo-tactile active palm with tactile array sensors to achieve robust grasping and fine manipulation. It features a gesture-conditioned retargeting framework for teleoperation, enabling complex tasks like syringe reorientation and small-object singulation.

card.one_liner: A tactile-reactive gripper using an active bi-modal palm for dexterous in-hand manipulation and teleoperation.
card.key_idea: Combines a 13-DOF three-finger structure with an actuated palm integrating vision and tactile sensing, supported by a gesture-conditioned retargeting framework for human-to-robot teleoperation.
card.evaluation: Tested on YCB objects, syringes, and small items (3mm). Achieved 93.3% grasping success and 65-70% success in complex manipulation tasks.
card.limitation: VR hand-tracking occlusions can cause unintentional finger release during teleoperation, leading to object slips.

slides.title: Catch, Throw, Repeat: Planning for Human-Robot Partner Juggling
slides.highlight: This work presents a planning and control architecture for synchronized multi-ball juggling between humans and robots, advancing physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A real-time planning system enabling a robot to perform synchronized multi-ball partner juggling with humans.
card.key_idea: Combines predictive Kalman-filter ball tracking, adaptive online trajectory optimization via multiple-shooting, and a state-machine coordination logic to manage catch-and-throw decisions.
card.evaluation: User study with 8 participants (beginner to expert); achieved 3-ball cascades and 100% success in single-ball trials. Results exceed previous benchmarks.
card.limitation: Performance is limited by timing pressure (minimum vacant phase duration) and lack of explicit spatial coordination to avoid inter-ball collisions.

slides.title: Foresight Residual RL for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation with Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING HANDOFF QUALITY IN LONG-HORIZON ASSEMBLY
slides.highlight: This work proposes Foresight Residual RL to improve long-horizon assembly by optimizing the quality of terminal states between subtasks, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill acquisition and human-AI intent alignment.

card.one_liner: Foresight Residual RL improves long-horizon robot manipulation by optimizing sub-task terminal states for downstream success.
card.key_idea: A visual foresight predictor estimates future success probabilities from terminal images, which then act as reward multipliers for residual RL policies trained via backward induction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a 3-phase wrench-nut assembly in Isaac Gym; achieved 85.6% full-task success, significantly outperforming standard residual RL (54.5%) and VLA baselines.
card.limitation: The residual scale must remain small to prevent distribution shift beyond the foresight predictor's training data.

slides.title: Data and Learning Where it Matters for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: TARGETED DATA COLLECTION FOR CONTACT-RICH TASKS
slides.highlight: This research introduces an automated data-collection scheme and offline deep reinforcement learning that focuses on critical contact segments while using traditional planning for free-space motion, significantly improving success rates in precision tasks.

card.one_liner: A modular framework achieving 96% success in contact-rich manipulation by targeting data collection at critical segments.
card.key_idea: Combines traditional motion planning for free-space movement with offline DRL trained on dense, autonomously collected data for the critical contact-rich task segment.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four real-world tasks; achieved 94-98% success rates using 2-2.5h of data, significantly outperforming end-to-end baselines (max 55%).
card.limitation: Requires tasks with clear sequential boundaries between free-space and contact-rich motion and relies on precise hardware for waypoint tracking.

slides.title: Scalable Open-Source Visuotactile Sensor for 6-Axis Contact Wrench Estimation in Tensegrity Robots
slides.tldr: OPEN-SOURCE VISUOTACTILE SENSOR FOR TENSEGRITY ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a scalable visuotactile sensor and neural network for 6-axis wrench estimation, enabling reliable contact detection and proprioception in tensegrity structures.

card.one_liner: An open-source visuotactile sensor for tensegrity robots enabling 6-axis contact wrench estimation and contact detection.
card.key_idea: Combines a fisheye camera and LED ring with a 3D-printed TPU/elastomer interface using gyroid-infill bonding; a residual MLP maps shear vector fields to 6D wrenches.
card.evaluation: Validated via KUKA robot and ATI F/T sensor (MSE 0.1531 static); integrated on a 12kg tensegrity robot to reliably detect ground contacts.
card.limitation: Torque estimation is less robust than force due to camera latency, processing delays, and lack of temporal modeling.
